newsitem.title: USA: Iraq unlikely to buy US wheat with oil money - trade.
newsitem.headline: Iraq unlikely to buy US wheat with oil money - trade.

text.p: Iraq will likely shun the United States when it begins buying wheat with proceeds from its pending oil sales, U.S. grain analysts and exporters said.
"I wouldn't expect the United States to be much of a participant," said one U.S. exporter.
He said lower-priced wheat is available elsewhere, plus lower shipping costs from European suppliers would be a consideration.
Analysts and exporters said Argentina, Canada, and Europe may be likely sellers because they can offer lower-priced wheat than the U.S.
"Europe is still the lowest-priced wheat for that part of the world," the exporter said.
White wheat is the lowest priced U.S. wheat at $158.00 per tonne, FOB, for January shipment versus $154.00 for EU wheat and $136 for Argentine. Canadian prices were unavailable.
Also, exporters said previous Iraq-U.S. tensions may discourage Iraq from buying U.S. grain. Also, exporters will be reluctant to sell to Iraq until the oil money is in hand.
Turkey hopes to supply most of the wheat to Iraq under the United Nations oil-for-food deal.

Iraq oil should start flowing December 15. Under the U.N. agreement, most of Iraq's oil will be shipped through a trans-Turkey pipeline, and Turkey's state oil refiner Tupras was expected to buy much of Iraq's oil.
Iraq was expected to import wheat worth $306 million and sugar worth $115 million under the deal, a Turkish foreign trade undersecretariat wrote in a note to Turkish exporters.
Assuming Turkish estimates are accurate, the $306 million Iraq may spend for wheat equates to about 1.8 million tonnes of U.S. wheat.

Joe Christopher, a grain analyst with U.S. brokerage firm LFG LLC, also expects Iraq to buy non-U.S. wheat. Further, Iraq's grain handling capacity is limited to about 200,000 to 250,000 tonnes a month, which would require Iraq importing the 1.8 million tonnes over many months.
"It is going to be stretched out over six months," he said of shipments into Iraq.
